keyAndScale.modalCharacter: E Dorian Funk with Single-Note Muted Raking

scalesUsed.application: John Frusciante's single-string percussive funk intro and verse riff

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C# - D
scalesUsed.application: The bright major sixth (C#) driving the chorus melody and chord progressions

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C - D
scalesUsed.application: The bridge chord movements through C major

mainProgression.description: Infectious funk-rock cadence built around single fretted notes raked across five muted strings

sectionProgressions.progression: Em - D - Bm - C (implied via single bass notes: E - D - B - C)
sectionProgressions.description: High-octane percussive funk rhythm with continuous right-hand strumming
Melodic full-chord strumming lifting into anthemic optimism ('Can't stop, addicted to the shindig')
Soaring, expressive wah-wah solo using sweet Dorian target notes

harmonicFunction: Root notes E → D → B → C outline standard minor funk movement while the top note (D on 7th fret 3rd string) remains a ringing melodic anchor
The percussive 'ghost-note' rakes create rhythmic polyphony, making a single guitar sound like a full percussion section
The chorus pivots to G major (♭III), opening up the sonic landscape into euphoric major harmony
Dorian character prevents the minor key from feeling gloomy, injecting infectious danceable swagger

techniques.name: Single-Note String Raking & Fretting-Hand Muting
techniques.description: Fretting exactly one target note while using all remaining fingers and thumb to mute the other 5 strings

notes: John Frusciante's definitive signature rhythm technique
The right hand strums aggressively across all six strings on every sixteenth note
Only the target note rings out—the other 5 strings produce dry, percussive 'chick' noises
Wrap the fretting thumb over the top to mute the low E string when playing higher notes
sequence: Fret 7th fret A string with index finger
Lay index finger flat across D, G, B, and high E strings to mute them
Wrap thumb over neck to mute low E string
Strum across all 6 strings with full force—only the 7th fret A string sounds
tips: Practice strumming all 6 strings while muting completely to test your fretting-hand muting seal
Keep the right hand in continuous sixteenth-note pendulum motion

techniques.name: Funky Thumb-Over Strumming Mechanics
techniques.description: Hendrix-inspired thumb wrap anchoring low bass notes while fingers dance across upper triads

notes: Enables lightning-fast transitions between percussive bass stabs and lyrical chord fills
Leaves the index, middle, and ring fingers free to fret melodic double stops
Creates an organic, loose funk feel that locks directly with Flea's slap bass
sequence: Fret low bass note with thumb over top of the neck
Add upper triad chord stabs on offbeats
tips: Keep the thumb relaxed against the neck—never squeeze with excess pressure
Listen to the snare drum to ensure offbeat stabs land in the pocket

sections.name: Iconic Intro Riff
sections.description: The world-famous funk-rock opening built on percussive string rakes across E, D, B, and C root positions.
sections.progression: E - D - B - C root notes
notes: Fret only one note at a time while muting all 5 remaining strings
Accent the target melody notes with pick velocity

sections.name: Chorus (Can't Stop, Addicted)
sections.description: Exploding into bright, singing major harmony with full open chord voicings.
notes: Switch from percussive raking to full open chord strumming
Lock tightly with Flea's punchy bassline
Keep the sixteenth-note strumming wrist loose and rhythmic

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: John Frusciante's soaring, lyrical guitar solo played through an Ibanez WH10 wah and Boss DS-2 distortion.
notes: Rock wah pedal slowly in time with the emotional contour
Accentuate the sweet major 6th (C#) Dorian color tones
End with wide, singing vibrato on the 12th fret root note

guitar.pickup: Neck pickup for the warm, rounded percussive rake tone

amp.recommended: Marshall Major 200W (Clean/Edge of breakup) & Marshall Silver Jubilee 2555

effects.distortion: Boss DS-2 Turbo Distortion (Turbo Mode ON for the solo)
effects.other: Ibanez WH10V1 Wah Pedal (essential for Frusciante solos), Dunlop Tortex 0.60mm pick

beginner.title: Chord Progression & Root Note Sequence
steps: Learn the 4-note bass root sequence: E (fret 7, string 5), D (fret 5, string 5), B (fret 7, string 6), C (fret 8, string 6)
Practice moving between these positions with a metronome at 70 BPM
Learn the G - D - Bm - C chorus chords

intermediate.title: Fretting-Hand Muting Technique
steps: Learn how to lay your fretting index finger flat to silence strings 1-4
Use your thumb over the neck to silence the low E string
Strum all 6 strings while isolating the single sounding target note

advanced.title: Full Speed Funk Groove & Solo
steps: Bring the percussive rake riff up to the album tempo of 91 BPM
Maintain continuous right-hand sixteenth-note pendulum motion without fatigue
Master the expressive wah-wah guitar solo with accurate pitch bends

commonMistakes: Trying to pick only the single string instead of strumming across all six muted strings
Letting adjacent strings ring openly because the fretting hand muting seal is loose
Stopping the right hand pendulum motion between chord shifts
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Muting seal check—strum all 6 strings on each note to verify zero unwanted notes ring
10 min: Slow drill of the 4-bar main riff at 65 BPM with metronome
15 min: Continuous rhythm play-along building up to 91 BPM
10 min: Wah pedal synchronization and solo phrasing
focusAreas: Flawless 5-string muting with fretting fingers and thumb
Locking into the pocket with kick drum and snare
metronomeWork: Start metronome at 65 BPM with sixteenth-note clicks
Ensure the right hand is in constant down-up-down-up pendulum motion
Increase by 4 BPM intervals up to target performance tempo of 91 BPM
